_note: Rule-based supportive guidance shown when the assessment is uncertain. English-only in this version (documented limitation). Never names or implies a condition.

guidance: Drink warm fluids regularly - water, soup, or warm tea

Avoid smoke, dust, and strong fumes

Reduce screen brightness, screen time, and loud noise where possible

Sip fluids frequently in small amounts rather than large quantities at once

Avoid oily, spicy, and heavy food for now
Watch for signs of dehydration such as passing very little urine or a dry mouth
Sip warm fluids to soothe the throat
Stay hydrated through the day
Rest your voice where you can
Rest and give your body time to recover
Stay hydrated through the day
Keep activity gentle and only as much as feels comfortable
Warm or cold compresses may help with localized aches
Keep the affected area clean and dry
Avoid scratching, which can worsen irritation or spread it
Wear loose, comfortable clothing
Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or bedding with others
Drink plenty of water through the day
Avoid holding urine for long periods
Maintain good personal hygiene

fallback_guidance: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Monitor your symptoms over the next 24-48 hours
See a doctor if symptoms worsen or persist beyond a few days
red_flags: Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
Confusion, fainting, or difficulty staying awake
Severe dehydration - passing very little urine, or dizziness on standing
Symptoms that are severe or getting worse quickly
A high fever that does not come down, or a fever lasting several days
disclaimer: This is general supportive guidance for comfort only. It does not diagnose or treat any condition. If you are unsure or feel worse, please consult a qualified doctor.
